mainTopic: Must we search again if a חולדה was seen taking חמץ? רבי זירא and רבא explain why we don't assume it ate the bread, and the גמרא tests רבא's rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי.
overview: The משנה rules that after בדיקת חמץ we do not worry that a חולדה dragged חמץ into a house that was already checked, because otherwise the worry would never end. The גמרא infers that if we actually saw the חולדה take bread, we must search again. It then asks why we don't just assume the חולדה ate the bread, since a משנה about מדורות הגוים assumes that weasels and pigs eat whatever they find. רבי זירא answers that a חולדה finishes meat completely but leaves pieces of bread behind. רבא answers differently. In the gentile's house everything is doubtful, but here we know for sure the bread was taken, and a ספק cannot override a ודאי. The גמרא challenges רבא's rule from a deceased חבר whose produce is presumed tithed. It gives two answers: a חזקה makes the tithing a ודאי, or, following רבי אושעיא, the produce may never have needed tithing, so it is ספק against ספק. The גמרא then begins a second challenge to רבא from a ברייתא about a maidservant in רימון who threw a stillborn into a pit, and that story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No worry that a weasel moved חמץ after the search
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that once a house has been checked, we do not worry that a חולדה dragged חמץ into it from somewhere else. Otherwise the worry would never end.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not worry that perhaps a weasel dragged חמץ from house to house, or from place to place. Because if so, we would also have to worry about courtyard to courtyard and city to city, and there would be no end to the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that a finished בדיקה can be trusted. We do not worry that a חולדה later brought חמץ into the checked area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is practical. If we worried about a weasel moving bread between houses, we would also have to worry about it moving bread between courtyards and even cities. No search could ever be trusted. So the חכמים set a limit: a completed search stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned / we don't worry
A weasel or marten, an animal known for dragging food around
There is no end to the matter

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a proper בדיקה is final. We do not invent endless 'what if' worries.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
We are not concerned that perhaps a weasel dragged [chametz]
from house to house, or from place to place,
phrases.notes: That is, into a house or spot that was already checked.

phrases.english: for if so, [we would worry] from courtyard to courtyard
and from city to city —
there would be no end to the matter.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: After בדיקה, we do not worry that a חולדה moved חמץ into the checked area, because otherwise the worry would never end.

steps.title: Inference: if we saw the weasel take bread, we must search
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that the leniency applies only when we did not see the חולדה take bread. If we did see it, we must search again.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason [we don't worry] is that we did not see it take [חמץ]. But if we saw it take [חמץ], we are concerned, and it requires searching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and draws out a limit. The leniency is only for a guess that the weasel moved bread. When we actually saw it carry bread, we worry and must search again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'שמא', meaning 'perhaps.' That word implies we are only dismissing an unseen possibility. Once the weasel was seen taking bread, it is no longer a guess, so a new בדיקה is needed. This inference becomes the target of the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But (in the opposite case)… — introduces the inferred flip side

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate ruling stated anywhere. It is a דיוק, an inference from the משנה's wording. The 'טעמא… הא…' pattern means 'only because of X; but without X, the opposite.'

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that we did not see it take [the bread];
but if we saw it take [the bread] — we are concerned,
and it requires searching.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלָא חֲזֵינָא דִּשְׁקַל, הָא חֲזֵינָא דִּשְׁקַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference (דיוק) from the משנה's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one saw a חולדה take חמץ, one must worry that it brought it into the house and search again.

steps.title: Why not assume the weasel ate the bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference: even if we saw the חולדה take bread, why not assume it simply ate it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us say it ate it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference from Step 2. If a weasel took bread, the likely outcome is that it ate it, so why should a new search be needed? Next, the גמרא will bring a source to back up this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge questions whether seeing the weasel take bread is really a reason to worry. If weasels normally eat food they grab, the bread is probably gone. Then the house needs no new בדיקה.

phrases.english: But why? Let us say it ate it!

steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that seeing a חולדה take bread requires a new בדיקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A weasel that takes bread most likely eats it, so there should be no reason to worry the bread is in the house.

steps.title: Source: gentile homes are treated as impure after forty days
steps.stepSummary: To support the challenge, the גמרא begins quoting a משנה. It rules that מדורות הגוים are טמא, and they need checking once a gentile has lived there for forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn [in a משנה]: The dwellings of gentiles are impure. And how long must he stay in a dwelling for the dwelling to require checking? Forty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a משנה from a completely different topic, טומאת מת, to support its challenge. This part only sets the scene. The key line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentiles were suspected of burying miscarried fetuses in their homes, so their homes were treated as possibly carrying טומאת מת. A fetus counts as such only after forty days of development. That is why the home needs checking only after forty days of living there.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn [in a משנה]? — introduces a source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the details of טומאה here. The גמרא only needs this משנה for one point, which comes next: animals eat what they find.

phrases.english: Didn't we learn [in a mishnah]:
The dwellings of gentiles are impure.
phrases.notes: Out of concern that a miscarried fetus was buried there.

phrases.english: And how long must he stay in a dwelling
for the dwelling to require checking —
forty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the challenge of Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a חולדה eats what it takes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in אהלות about מדורות הגוים (opening portion).

steps.title: Key line: places a weasel or pig can reach need no checking
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues: the rule applies even if the gentile has no wife. Any place a חולדה or pig can reach needs no checking, because they would have eaten what was there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though he has no wife. And any place where a weasel or a pig can walk does not need checking!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the challenge. The משנה assumes a weasel eats whatever it finds, so by the same logic we should assume it ate the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line 'even though he has no wife' shows the חכמים made the rule uniform, not case by case. The key point is the last line: we rely on the חזקה that animals eat what they find. If so, a weasel seen taking bread should be assumed to have eaten it. Then the inference of Step 2 is in trouble.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge stands: the משנה in אהלות assumes a חולדה eats what it finds. So why should seeing it take bread require a new search? Step 6 (רבי זירא) and Step 7 (רבא) answer this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key distinction the גמרא will need to make: why we assume a weasel eats in one case but not in the other.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: And [this applies] even though he has no wife.
And any place where a weasel or a pig
can walk —
does not need checking!
phrases.notes: Because the animal would have eaten anything buried there. So too here, the weasel should be assumed to have eaten the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁחוּלְדָּה וַחֲזִיר יְכוֹלִין לַהֲלוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted source and delivers the point that powers the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that a חולדה should be presumed to have eaten the bread.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in אהלות: any place a חולדה or pig can reach needs no checking.

steps.title: Meat Gets Eaten Completely, Bread Does Not
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא resolves the contradiction: the משנה of מדורות הגוים deals with flesh, which a חולדה finishes entirely, while our case deals with bread, which a חולדה leaves pieces of.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: There is no difficulty. This case is about meat, and that case is about bread. With meat, the animal leaves nothing over. With bread, it leaves some over.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge from Step 3. He explains why one case says 'assume it ate it' and the other says 'search again.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry in מדורות הגוים is a buried נפל (a stillborn), which is flesh, and a חולדה eats flesh completely. Bread is different, because a חולדה tends to leave crumbs or pieces behind. So when we see it take bread, some חמץ may still be left somewhere, and we must search again.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is a standard opening for resolving a contradiction.
Meat or flesh. Here it means the נפל that might be buried in a gentile's house.
Bread, meaning the חמץ in our case.
It leaves over, meaning it leaves remnants behind.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said,
It is not difficult:
This case is about meat,
phrases.notes: The משנה of מדורות הגוים, where the concern is a buried stillborn.

phrases.english: and that case is about bread.
phrases.notes: Our case of the חולדה and the חמץ.

phrases.english: With meat, it does not leave any over.
With bread, it does leave some over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 3-5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by type of food (חילוק between meat and bread)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve a חולדה, so they should follow the same rule and we should always assume it ate what it took.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat is eaten completely, but bread leaves remnants, so bread requires a new search.

steps.title: רבא: A Doubt Cannot Override a Certainty
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the comparison between the cases. In מדורות הגוים everything is doubtful, but here we know for certain the bread was taken, and a ספק does not override a ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What kind of comparison is this? There, it makes sense: maybe there was a stillborn and maybe there was not. And even if there was one, maybe the animal ate it. But here, where we definitely saw it take the bread, who says it ate it? It is a doubt against a certainty, and a doubt does not override a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own, different answer to the contradiction. He says the two cases were never really alike to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מדורות הגוים there are two doubts stacked together: maybe nothing was ever buried there, and even if something was, maybe it was eaten. In our case, the bread's presence is certain (ודאי), and only its being eaten is doubtful (ספק). A ספק is not strong enough to cancel a ודאי, so we must search.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Used to reject a comparison as unfair.
Granted. It concedes one case before contrasting it with another.
Say, meaning you can assume a possibility.
A doubt does not take you out of a certainty.

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי is a major rule throughout ש״ס for deciding doubtful cases.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not adding to רבי זירא. He gives a separate explanation, so according to רבא, even with meat we would search again if we saw the חולדה take it.

phrases.english: Rava said: What is this comparison?
Granted, there,
phrases.notes: In the case of מדורות הגוים.

phrases.english: say there was a stillborn, or say there was not.
And even if you say there was one,
say the animal ate it.
But here, where we definitely saw that it took the bread,
who says that it ate it?
It is a doubt against a certainty,
and a doubt does not override a certainty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the basis of the comparison and offers an alternative resolution to רבי זירא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by level of certainty (ספק ספיקא vs. ספק against ודאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since we assume a חולדה ate things in מדורות הגוים, we should assume the same here.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the bread's presence is certain, and a doubt that it was eaten cannot override that certainty.

steps.title: Challenge from the חבר Who Died with Produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule from a ברייתא. Produce left by a deceased חבר is presumed tithed, even though it was certainly untithed and its tithing is only doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that a doubt does not override a certainty? But a ברייתא teaches: if a חבר died and left a storehouse full of produce, even produce from that same day, it is presumed tithed. Here the produce was certainly untithed at first, and it is only doubtful whether it was tithed, yet the doubt comes and overrides the certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's principle that a ספק cannot override a ודאי. It brings a case where a doubt seems to win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes the stored produce was definitely טבל (untithed) once its processing was finished, so that is the ודאי. Whether the חבר tithed it before dying is only a ספק. Yet the ברייתא lets us treat it as tithed, which looks like a ספק overriding a ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא. It introduces a source that contradicts something.
A person trusted to be careful with מעשרות and טהרה.
Literally 'of their day,' meaning produce brought in only that day.

phrases.english: And does a doubt really not override a certainty?!
But it was taught in a baraita:
A ḥaver who died and left behind
a storehouse full of produce,
and even if the produce was brought in that very day,
it is presumed to be properly tithed.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּוַדַּאי טְבִילִי הָנֵי פֵּירֵי,
phrases.english: But here, this produce was certainly untithed,
and it is doubtful whether it was tithed or not tithed,
and the doubt comes and overrides the certainty!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי?! וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle רבא used in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of the חבר's produce, the doubt that it was tithed overrides the certainty that it was טבל, which contradicts רבא's rule.

steps.title: A חבר's Produce Is Certainly Tithed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חבר case is a ודאי against a ודאי, because רבי חנינא חוזאה established a חזקה that a חבר never lets untithed produce leave his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is a certainty against a certainty, because the produce is certainly tithed, as רבי חנינא חוזאה taught. רבי חנינא חוזאה said: We may presume that a חבר does not let anything untithed leave his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's rule. It shows that the חבר case does not really involve a doubt at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the חזקה about a חבר, the tithing counts as a certainty, not a doubt. So it is a ודאי (it was טבל) against another ודאי (a חבר surely tithed it), not a ספק against a ודאי. רבא's rule that a mere ספק cannot override a ודאי stands unbroken.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption, an assumption treated as reliable.
From under his hand, meaning out of his possession or control.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a doubt cannot cancel a certainty. That is why seeing a חולדה take bread requires a new search. A strong חזקה, like the one about a חבר, counts as a certainty and can override an earlier certainty.

phrases.english: There, it is a certainty against a certainty,
for the produce is certainly tithed,
in accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina Ḥoza'a.
For Rabbi Ḥanina Ḥoza'a said:
There is a presumption about a ḥaver
that he does not let leave his possession
anything that is not properly tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8 and defends רבא's principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the 'doubt' is really a certainty because of a חזקה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whether the חבר tithed the produce is only a doubt, so a ספק is overriding a ודאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חזקה about a חבר makes the tithing certain, so it is ודאי against ודאי, and רבא's rule stands.

steps.title: Second answer: the deceased חבר case is doubt against doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another answer to the challenge from the deceased חבר. That case is really a ספק against a ספק, because the produce may never have needed tithing in the first place, following רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: it is a doubt against a doubt. Perhaps one could say that from the start the produce was never untithed, following רבי אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to answer the question from step 8. It says the חבר's produce case has no certainty on either side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 assumed the produce was certainly untithed (a ודאי). This answer questions that assumption: maybe the produce was never obligated in tithes at all. If so, both sides are doubtful, and רבא's rule that a ספק does not override a ודאי is not challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces an alternative answer
A doubt against a doubt, so neither side is certain

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not replace the rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי. It agrees with that rule and only says the חבר case never had a ודאי to begin with.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it is a doubt against a doubt,
perhaps one could say that from the start
it was not untithed produce at all,
in line with Rabbi Oshaya.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: סָפֵק וְסָפֵק הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge in step 8, in place of step 9's חזקה answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: denies that one side is a ודאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The deceased חבר's produce was certainly untithed, so a ספק seemed to override a ודאי
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce may never have needed tithing, so the case is ספק against ספק and does not challenge רבא

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: grain brought in with its chaff for animals is exempt from tithes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אושעיא's ruling as the source for the second answer. A person may bring his grain in while still in its chaff, so his animal can eat it without tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אושעיא said: A person may use a clever method with his grain. He brings it in while it is still in its chaff, so that his animal can eat from it, and it is exempt from tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אושעיא's ruling to support the claim that the חבר's produce may never have needed tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain only becomes obligated in tithes once its processing is finished. If it is brought in still in its chaff and fed to animals, it never becomes obligated. So the חבר's stored produce might have been in that state, and there is no certainty that it was ever טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses a legal method to avoid an obligation
Chaff, the husks around the grain

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that tithing depends on how and when the produce was processed. That is enough to make the original obligation itself doubtful.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Oshaya said:
A person may use a clever method with his grain,
and bring it in while still in its chaff,
so that his animal may eat from it,
and it is exempt from tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 10's claim
steps.raayaObject: That the deceased חבר's produce may never have been obligated in tithes
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אושעיא's ruling that grain brought in with its chaff for animal food is exempt from tithes
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the deceased חבר: (1) a חזקה makes the tithing a ודאי, so it is ודאי against ודאי; (2) the produce may never have needed tithing, so it is ספק against ספק. Either way, רבא's rule stands.

steps.title: New challenge to רבא: the maidservant in רימון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבא's rule again, this time from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה tells of a maidservant of a violent man in רימון who threw a stillborn baby into a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it true that a doubt does not override a certainty? But it was taught in a ברייתא that רבי יהודה said: There was an incident with the maidservant of a certain violent man in רימון, who threw a stillborn baby into a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attack on רבא's rule and begins quoting a ברייתא story. The story continues on the next amud, where the challenge will become clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and is it true that a ספק does not override a ודאי?!' signal that a source is about to show a case where a ספק does override a ודאי. The setup here is a certain fact: a stillborn baby was thrown into a pit. The ruling that follows will be used against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that teaches a ruling

phrases.english: And does a doubt really not override a certainty?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back on רבא here.

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with the maidservant of a certain violent man
in Rimon, who threw a stillborn baby into a pit,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא from the חבר case, the גמרא raises a new challenge to the same rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule from step 7 that a ספק does not override a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא will describe a case with a certain fact (a stillborn was thrown into a pit) that is still decided by a doubt, which suggests a ספק can override a ודאי
